[MUJAHID:v1p315/r1] MUJAHID, d. 104 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid says the signs they saw included the torn back of Joseph's shirt.
[MUQATIL:12:34-35/r2] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The torn shirt from behind proved Joseph innocent, but the husband imprisoned him after Zulaykha asked to keep him from approaching her.
[MUQATIL:12:34-35/r3] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | reports | In prison Joseph comforted mourners, reassured the frightened, cared for the sick, and interpreted dreams; he described his lineage as a prophet through Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham.
[FARRA:v2p43/r4] FARRA, d. 207 · author | holds | The signs of Joseph's innocence were that the shirt was torn from behind; the lām in ليَسجننه marks an oath or speech-like assertion, also used after الظن and العلم. | mentions 12:26, 12:36, 12:80
[ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p323/r1] ABDURRAZZAQ, d. 211 · قتادة | reports | Qatada says the signs were the women's hand wounds and the shirt torn from behind.
[AKHFASH:v1p397/r3] AKHFASH, d. 215 · author | holds | The emphatic nūn in ليسجننه is licensed because the clause can host an interrogative, as in asking which of them will take someone.
[TAB-FULL:v13p147/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | The singular verb in 'it appeared to them' refers to the Aziz, who is not named or individually specified; al-Tabari compares the construction with a report where one person speaks as 'the people.' | mentions 3:173
[TAB-FULL:v13p147/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | After seeing signs of Yusuf's innocence, they reversed their apparent decision to release him and decided to imprison him; the signs included the rear shirt tear, scratches on the face, and women's cut hands.
[TAB-FULL:v13p147/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas identifies the signs as the tear in Yusuf's shirt and scratches on the woman's face.
[TAB-FULL:v13p147/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid identifies the sign as the tear in Yusuf's shirt from behind.
[TAB-FULL:v13p147/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · قتادة | reports | Qatada says the signs were the women's hand wounds and the tear in Yusuf's shirt.
[TAB-FULL:v13p147/r6] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · السدي | reports | Al-Suddi lists the shirt and the women's cut hands among the signs.
[TAB-FULL:v13p150/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | They intended to keep Yusuf imprisoned until they chose their next course; al-Tabari says God made this confinement a punishment for Yusuf's prior inclination toward the woman and an expiation.
[TAB-FULL:v13p150/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas relates three lapses: Yusuf's inclination led to prison, asking the cupbearer for help prolonged it, and his brothers' accusation of theft led to a brother's accusation against him. | mentions 12:42, 12:70, 12:77
[TAB-FULL:v13p150/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · السدي | reports | Al-Suddi says the Aziz's wife asked her husband either to let her leave and explain herself or imprison Yusuf because he was telling people she had solicited him.
[TAB-FULL:v13p150/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · أهل العربية من البصرة | reports | One Basran grammatical explanation says the emphatic lām and nūn in la-yasjununnahu occur where an interrogative construction with ay would otherwise appear.
[TAB-FULL:v13p150/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · بعض أهل العربية | rejects | Some grammarians reject the interrogative explanation: the lām is an oath, since an emphatic nūn does not follow a question such as 'will you stand?'.
[TAB-FULL:v13p150/r6] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · نحوي من الكوفة | reports | A Kufan grammarian says bada lahum carries the sense of 'they said/decided,' and speech can introduce either an oath or an interrogative, licensing the construction.
[TAB-FULL:v13p150/r7] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · عكرمة | reports | Ikrima interprets the time until which Yusuf was imprisoned as seven years.
[ZAJJAJ:v3p104/r1] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | Badā is intransitive here with no expressed subject; Arabs say badā lī badāʾan when an opinion changes, usually omitting the noun because the context makes the change clear. 
[ZAJJAJ:v3p104/r2] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | The decision was to imprison Joseph; the master had first ordered only that he be avoided, then changed his mind. 
[IBNABIHATIM:v7p2139#2/r1] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · ابن عباس | reports | The signs included the shirt's tear and knife marks; the wife warned that unless Joseph were imprisoned people would believe him.
[IBNABIHATIM:v7p2139#2/r2] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · عكرمة | reports | The signs were the torn shirt and the women's scratched faces.
[IBNABIHATIM:v7p2139#2/r3] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · السدي | reports | The wife told her husband the Hebrew servant had exposed her, and asked either to leave and defend herself or to have him imprisoned; the signs included the torn shirt and cut hands.
[IBNABIHATIM:v7p2139#2/r4] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · عبد الرحمن بن زيد | reports | One of the signs was what the nursing woman said in the courtyard.
[IBNABIHATIM:v7p2139#2/r5] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · ابن اسحاق | reports | The signs showed Joseph's innocence, including the shirt torn from behind.
[IBNABIHATIM:v7p2139#2/r6] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · ابن عباس | reports | Joseph was punished three times; the first punishment was imprisonment because of his desire for her.
[IBNABIHATIM:v7p2139#2/r7] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · وهب بن منبه | reports | Gabriel told Joseph in prison that God called him righteous because grief, slavery, and imprisonment had not led him to obey his mistress in sin; God counted him among the purified and righteous.
[IBNABIHATIM:v7p2140/r1] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · ابن عباس | reports | The word “ḥīn” can mean morning or evening.
[IBNABIHATIM:v7p2140/r2] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · عكرمة | reports | In a vow to cut off a boy's hand and imprison him for a period, the ruling was not to cut the hand and to imprison him for a year.
[IBNABIHATIM:v7p2140/r3] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · سعيد بن جبير | reports | The word “ḥīn” can mean six months; Ṭāriq is reported to agree.
[IBNABIHATIM:v7p2140/r4] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · عكرمة | reports | Another reported interpretation of “ḥīn” is seven years.
[IBNABIHATIM:v7p2140/r5] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · عكرمة | reports | For a vow to imprison a slave for a “ḥīn,” some periods can be fulfilled and others cannot; the unbounded period is the Qur'anic “until a time.”
[NAHHAS:v2p329/r1] NAHHAS, d. 338 · سيبويه | reports | Sibawayh makes ليسجننه the subject of بدا; Muhammad ibn Yazid supplies a hidden noun, another reading means something new became known.
[IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p343/r2] IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB, d. 392 · عمر | reports | ʿUmar reports hearing a reader say عتى حين, asks who taught him, then instructs Ibn Masʿūd to teach Quraysh Arabic rather than Hudhayl's dialect.
[IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p343/r3] IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB, d. 392 · author | holds | The consonants in عتى and حتى can interchange because their articulation points are close; the more commonly used form is preferable, though the variant is permissible.
[THALABI:v5p220/r10] THALABI, d. 427 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas counts three lapses by Joseph: the episode leading to prison, asking the cupbearer to remember him, and accusing his brothers of theft.
[THALABI:v5p220/r3] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | The officials who saw signs of Joseph’s innocence nevertheless decided to imprison him for a time.
[THALABI:v5p220/r4] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | The signs of innocence included the shirt torn from behind, scratches to the face, and the women cutting their hands.
[THALABI:v5p220/r5] THALABI, d. 427 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farra says the lām in the oath and in reported present-tense speech is used because both expressions carry the sense of speech and oath.
[THALABI:v5p220/r6] THALABI, d. 427 · عكرمة | reports | Ikrima says the phrase until a time means nine years.
[THALABI:v5p220/r7] THALABI, d. 427 · الكلبي | reports | Al-Kalbi says Joseph remained imprisoned five years.
[THALABI:v5p220/r8] THALABI, d. 427 · السدي | reports | Al-Suddi says the wife complained Joseph had publicly accused her of seducing him and asked either to leave to defend herself or for him to be imprisoned too.
[THALABI:v5p220/r9] THALABI, d. 427 · author | reports | God made prison a purification for Joseph’s desire toward the woman and an expiation for his lapse.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p34#2/r1] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | The signs they saw may be the torn shirt and the women's cut hands or Yusuf's evident chastity and beauty, which made them call him an angel rather than a human.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p34#2/r2] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · سعيد بن جبير | reports | The term of imprisonment was six months according to Sa'id ibn Jubayr, seven years according to Ikrima, or an unspecified period according to many commentators.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p34#2/r3] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · السدي | reports | Al-Suddi says al-Aziz's wife accused the Hebrew slave of slandering her and demanded either divorce so she could defend herself or that he be imprisoned as she had been; her husband jailed Yusuf.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p108#2/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · وهب | reports | Zulaykhā complained that Joseph had disgraced her publicly and asked to leave to defend herself or have him jailed as she had been; the governor and his associates decided to imprison him.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p108#2/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · السدي | reports | Al-Suddī shares the report that Zulaykhā demanded Joseph be jailed because he had exposed her.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p108#2/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · المفسرون | reports | The signs of Joseph's innocence were the shirt torn from behind, the scratched face, and the sage's ruling against her, including her admission that it was the women's plot.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p108#2/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · قتادة | reports | Qatāda includes the women's cutting their hands among the signs; al-Wāḥidī questions how that demonstrates Joseph's innocence.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p108#2/r5] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | One grammatical analysis supplies a hidden subject for بدا, i

[WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | In ʿAṭāʾ's report, the imprisonment lasted until the gossip and scandal in the city died down.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | In al-Kalbī's report, the period was five years.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · سفيان | reports | Sufyān and ʿIkrima say Joseph was imprisoned for seven years.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r5] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · عكرمة | reports | ʿIkrima agrees with Sufyān that the period was seven years.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r6] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · مقاتل بن سليمان | reports | Muqātil b. Sulaymān says Joseph remained imprisoned for twelve years.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r7] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | The governor agreed to his wife's request and imprisoned Joseph despite knowing he was innocent.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r8] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · المفسرون | reports | The commentators say God made the imprisonment a purification for Joseph from his desire for the woman and an expiation for his lapse.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p110/r9] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن الأنباري | reports | God left the period unspecified to honor scholars and direct people to them to solve interpretive difficulties.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r2] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | After seeing signs of Joseph's innocence, the ruler and his companions decided to imprison him until the public blame stopped.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r3] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | The ruler's wife said Joseph had exposed her by telling people she had tried to seduce him, so she wanted him imprisoned until gossip ended.
[JISHUMI:v5p3637/r7] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Badw means appearing or becoming visible; badāʾ in opinion is a change of mind as new opinions appear.
[JISHUMI:v5p3637/r8] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The final nūn in ليكونا is emphatic and may be light or heavy; the nūn in ليسجنن is heavy, and pause forms differ from connected speech, as in لنسفعا.
[JISHUMI:v5p3641/r1] JISHUMI, d. 494 · عكرمة | reports | Until a time may mean seven years according to ʿIkrima, ten years according to al-Kalbī, or a long period according to al-Aṣamm.
[JISHUMI:v5p3641/r2] JISHUMI, d. 494 · أبو علي | reports | Other explanations say the imprisonment lasted until the rulers decided what to do, or until talk of the woman faded and Joseph was cut off from people.
[JISHUMI:v5p3641/r6] JISHUMI, d. 494 · الأصم | reports | Al-Aṣamm says the women imposed the apparent punishment of imprisonment but did not succeed in corrupting Joseph's religion.
[JISHUMI:v5p3641/r7] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Their plotting and imprisonment were their own acts, not created by God.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p239#2/r3] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | The Aziz and his associates first intended merely to order Joseph to be ignored, then decided to imprison him after seeing the signs of his innocence.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p239#2/r4] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | The signs included the torn shirt, the child’s speech, and the women cutting their hands and losing their senses.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p239#2/r5] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · عطاء | reports | Ata says the prison term lasted until people stopped talking about the affair.

[BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p239#2/r7] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · الكلبي | reports | Al-Kalbi says Joseph remained imprisoned five years.

[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441/r1] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | The implicit subject of bada is a newly formed opinion, namely their decision to imprison Yusuf; the pronoun refers to the Aziz and his household.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441/r2] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | The signs were evidence of Yusuf's innocence; the wife nevertheless persuaded and controlled her compliant husband, who followed her plan to imprison and humiliate him.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441/r3] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | reports | The wife either gave up hope that Yusuf would obey her or hoped prison would humble him and make him compliant.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441/r4] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · الحسن | reports | Al-Ḥasan's reading latasjunannahu addresses the Aziz and those around him, or addresses the Aziz alone deferentially.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441/r5] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | Ḥattā ḥīn means for a period, apparently the duration the wife proposed while waiting to see what Yusuf would do.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441/r6] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · ابن مسعود | reports | Ibn Masʿud's reading ʿattā ḥīn is a Hudhayl dialect form.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441/r7] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · عمر | reports | After hearing a man recite ʿattā ḥīn, ʿUmar asked his teacher and wrote Ibn Masʿud to teach Quraysh speech rather than Hudhayl speech.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p242#2/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | reports | After Joseph refused sin, the wife of al-Aziz allegedly told her husband that the Hebrew boy had publicly disgraced her and was explaining matters on his own terms; she demanded either release so she could defend herself and accuse him, or his imprisonment while she remained confined. They then chose prison.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p242#2/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says Joseph was put on a donkey, a drum was beaten, and he was announced through Egypt's markets as a Hebrew who desired his master and deserved prison; Abu Salih says Ibn Abbas wept whenever recounting it.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p242#2/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | بدا means appeared, with a deleted subject estimated as بدو or رأي; the plural لهم refers to the king alone because the decision involved consultation, and ليسجننه is an oath clause.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p242#2/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · سيبويه | reports | Sibawayh's explicit position is that ليسجننه cannot be the grammatical subject of بدا, since a sentence cannot be its subject; the claim that it is the subject is wrong, and the sentence instead explains the omitted subject.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p242#2/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · مجاهد وغيره | reports | Interpreters identify the signs as the torn shirt; Ikrima says Joseph's scratched face accompanied the shirt episode, and al-Suddi says the women cut their hands.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p242#2/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The point is that they decided on prison after signs had exonerated Joseph; scratched faces and cut hands do not prove innocence, whereas the shirt report does. [IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p242#2/r7] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Alternatively, 'after they saw the signs' may mean that the overall circumstances showed Joseph was innocent, without identifying any one specific sign.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Ḥīn means an unspecified span of time, potentially short or long; the Qur’an uses it in both senses.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · عكرمة | reports | He takes ḥīn here to mean seven years.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | reports | Another reported interpretation takes the period as one year; the author relates these durations to what was disclosed during Joseph’s imprisonment.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · عمر بن الخطاب | reports | Umar heard a Hudhayli reading عتى حين and wrote Ibn Masud to teach people in Quraysh Arabic rather than Hudhayl’s dialect.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas counts three slips by Joseph: the episode with her, asking the cupbearer to remember him, and accusing the brothers of theft, which prompted the reply about Benjamin. | mentions 12:24, 12:42, 12:70, 12:77
[TABRISI:12:34-35/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Although the women were previously mentioned, the masculine plural 'them' refers to the king; another reading takes it as Zuleikha and her helpers, with masculine agreement for a mixed group.

[TABRISI:12:34-35/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | Another interpretation takes the signs as evidence that the women had despaired of obtaining Yusuf.
[TABRISI:12:34-35/r5] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The grammatical subject of بدا is omitted and understood as بداء; the decision that appeared was the decision to imprison him.
